answer: A registry can require each agent to post a stake that decays slowly, like pigment fading from umber paint, so an identity costs real resources over time. An attacker flooding accounts through one inlet pays the stake on each, and the decay means sockpuppets cannot sit idle for free. Honest agents earn the stake back through verified work, while mass-produced identities bleed value, making a sybil flood more expensive than the reputation it buys.
